findings.why_it_matters: inspect_composer takes blocks[-1] unconditionally. A composer block ends at the first row that is not a continuation, and a new block starts at every glyph-led row, so an operator draft that SPANS a glyph-led row is split: the earlier rows holding the text stop being the box, and a trailing glyph-led row that is empty becomes the box. guard_pane_before_write then takes the EMPTY branch at launcher.py:802-805, which sets the receipt's input_box to 'empty' and returns WITHOUT appending any note, and launch() proceeds to send() at launcher.py:1401. The operator's unsent text is then concatenated with the dispatched task and submitted -- the exact harm the feature exists to prevent. Two things make this worse than the documented fail-open trade. First, the receipt records an affirmative false claim, 'empty', rather than one of the five inconclusive causes the design already carries; unlike every inconclusive state it also writes no note at all, so nothing on the run record hints that the read was ambiguous. Second, SKILL.md:43 enumerates the fail-open states as unclassifiable, not_found, unsupported_vendor, read_failed and read_timeout, so an operator reading the contract believes an 'empty' receipt means the box was empty. The plain-marker vendors are the easy case: agy and qwen use a bare greater-than sign, so a draft ending in a blank markdown quote row collapses to EMPTY. For claude the shape needs a glyph-led final row, which is what an operator gets by pasting a Claude prompt echo -- the checked-in fixture shows Claude renders its echoes with the same glyph. The suite pins the opposite behaviour as intended at test_launcher_contract.py:627, so this is a deliberate trade rather than an oversight; it is nonetheless an undisclosed one that produces a false receipt field, and the design already owns an 'unclassifiable' bucket that this case belongs in.
